title.raw: 卷58 志三十三 地理五 江苏

translations.literal: Treatise thirty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 33

translations.literal: Geography five.
translations.idiomatic: Geography 5

translations.literal: Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangsu

sentences.zh: 江蘇：禹貢揚及徐、豫三州之域。

translations.literal: Jiangsu: the territory of the Yang, Xu, and Yu provinces in the Yugong.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangsu comprised the domains of the Yang, Xu, and Yu regions described in the Tribute of Yu.

translations.literal: Under the Ming it was Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming dynasty it formed Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 清順治二年改江南省，設布政使司，置兩江總督轄江南、江西，駐江寧。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi in the Qing it was changed to Jiangnan Province; a provincial administration commission was established; a governor-general of the Two Jiangs was placed in charge of Jiangnan and Jiangxi, stationed at Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In Qing Shunzhi 2 it was renamed Jiangnan Province, a provincial administration commission was set up, and a governor-general of the Two Jiangs was appointed over Jiangnan and Jiangxi with his seat at Jiangning.

translations.literal: A Huai-Yang governor-general was also established, and soon abolished.
translations.idiomatic: A Huai-Yang governor-general was also appointed but soon abolished.

translations.literal: And a Jiangning governor.
translations.idiomatic: A Jiangning governor was added as well.

translations.literal: Administered from Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Its administrative seat was at Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 又設鳳廬安徽巡撫，尋裁。

translations.literal: A Feng-Lu Anhui governor was also established, and soon abolished.
translations.idiomatic: A Feng-Lu Anhui governor was also appointed but soon abolished.

sentences.zh: 十八年，分府九：安慶、徽州、寧國、池州、太平、廬州、鳳陽、淮安、揚州，直隸州四：徐、滁、和、廣德，屬安徽，江南左布政使領之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, nine prefectures were divided off: Anqing, Huizhou, Ningguo, Chizhou, Taiping, Luzhou, Fengyang, Huai'an, and Yangzhou; four directly administered prefectures: Xu, Chu, He, and Guangde — these belonged to Anhui and were led by the left provincial administration commissioner of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18, nine prefectures—Anqing, Huizhou, Ningguo, Chizhou, Taiping, Luzhou, Fengyang, Huai'an, and Yangzhou—and four directly administered prefectures (Xu, Chu, He, and Guangde) were assigned to Anhui under the left provincial administration commissioner of Jiangnan.

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi, Anhui established a governor.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 1 a governor was appointed for Anhui.

sentences.zh: 三年，分江北按察使往治。

translations.literal: In the third year, the Jiangbei provincial judge was separated to administer there.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 the Jiangbei provincial judge was posted separately to govern the region.

sentences.zh: 五年，揚州、淮安、徐州復隸江南。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Yangzhou, Huai'an, and Xuzhou again were subordinate to Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 Yangzhou, Huai'an, and Xuzhou were restored to Jiangnan jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 六年，江南更今名，改左布政使為安徽布政使司，駐江寧。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Jiangnan took its present name; the left provincial administration commissioner was changed to the Anhui provincial administration commission, stationed at Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 Jiangnan received its present name; the left commissioner became the Anhui provincial administration commission, seated at Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 右布政使為江蘇布政使司，治蘇州。

translations.literal: The right provincial administration commissioner became the Jiangsu provincial administration commission, administering from Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The right commissioner became the Jiangsu provincial administration commission, headquartered at Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 統江寧、蘇州、常州、松江、鎮江、揚州、淮安府七，徐州直隸州一。

translations.literal: It governed seven prefectures — Jiangning, Suzhou, Changzhou, Songjiang, Zhenjiang, Yangzhou, and Huai'an — and one directly administered prefecture, Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: It oversaw seven prefectures—Jiangning, Suzhou, Changzhou, Songjiang, Zhenjiang, Yangzhou, and Huai'an—and one directly administered prefecture, Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年，升太倉、邳、海、通四州為直隸州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng, four prefectures — Taicang, Pi, Hai, and Tong — were promoted to directly administered prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 2 Taicang, Pi, Hai, and Tong were each promoted to directly administered prefecture status.

sentences.zh: 十一年，徐州升府，邳還為州，屬之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Xuzhou was promoted to a prefecture; Pi reverted to prefectural status and was subordinate to it.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 Xuzhou was raised to prefectural rank and Pi was demoted again to a dependent prefecture under it.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十五年，移安徽布政使司安慶，增設江寧布政使司，析江寧、淮安、徐、揚四府，通、海二直隸州屬之，與江蘇布政使司對治。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Qianlong, the Anhui provincial administration commission was moved to Anqing; the Jiangning provincial administration commission was added; Jiangning, Huai'an, Xu, and Yangzhou four prefectures and Tong and Hai two directly administered prefectures were detached to belong to it, facing the Jiangsu provincial administration commission in paired administration.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 25 the Anhui commission moved to Anqing and a Jiangning commission was added, taking Jiangning, Huai'an, Xuzhou, and Yangzhou prefectures plus Tong and Hai directly administered prefectures so that it administered in parallel with the Jiangsu commission.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，增海門直隸廳，屬江寧。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, Haimen directly administered subprefecture was added, subordinate to Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In year 32 Haimen directly administered subprefecture was created under Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 光緒三十年，又設江淮巡撫，駐清江浦。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Guangxu, a Jianghuai governor was again established, stationed at Qingjiangpu.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 30 a Jianghuai governor was again appointed, stationed at Qingjiangpu.

translations.literal: Soon the former arrangement was restored.
translations.idiomatic: The post was soon abolished and the former arrangement restored.

sentences.zh: 廣九百五十里，袤千一百三十里，積三十七萬二千五十四方里。

translations.literal: Its width was nine hundred fifty li, its length one thousand one hundred thirty li, and its area three hundred seventy-two thousand fifty-four square li.
translations.idiomatic: It measured 950 li from east to west and 1,130 li from north to south, with an area of 372,054 square li.

sentences.zh: 北極高三十一度五分至三十五度十分。

translations.literal: North polar altitude ranged from thirty-one degrees five minutes to thirty-five degrees ten minutes.
translations.idiomatic: Latitude ranged from 31°05′ to 35°10′ north.

sentences.zh: 京師偏東五分至五度三分。

translations.literal: East of the capital ranged from five minutes to five degrees three minutes.
translations.idiomatic: Longitude lay between 0°05′ and 5°03′ east of the capital.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年，編戶三百二十一萬三千四百八十三，口九百三十五萬六千七百五十五。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuantong, registered households numbered three million two hundred thirteen thousand four hundred eighty-three, and population nine million three hundred fifty-six thousand seven hundred fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 3 there were 3,213,483 registered households and a population of 9,356,755.

sentences.zh: 領府八，直隸州三，直隸廳一，州三，廳四，縣六十。

translations.literal: It governed eight prefectures, three directly administered prefectures, one directly administered subprefecture, three prefectures, four subprefectures, and sixty counties.
translations.idiomatic: Its administrative units comprised eight prefectures, three directly administered prefectures, one directly administered subprefecture, three dependent prefectures, four subprefectures, and sixty counties.

translations.literal: Jiangning Prefecture: Vital, Busy, and Difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangning Prefecture: Vital, Busy, and Difficult.

translations.literal: Subordinate to the Jiangning circuit.
translations.idiomatic: It belonged to the Jiangning circuit intendancy.

translations.literal: Under the Ming, Yingtian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming it was Yingtian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 江寧布政、交涉、提學三使，江安糧儲、江南勸業、巡警、鹽法四道，江寧將軍、副都統，織造兼督龍江西新稅關駐。

translations.literal: The Jiangning provincial administration, foreign affairs, and education commissioners; the Jiang-An grain transport, Jiangnan industrial promotion, constabulary, and salt control circuits; the Jiangning general and deputy lieutenant-general; and the weaving office concurrently supervising the Longjiang western new customs post were stationed there.
translations.idiomatic: Stationed there were the Jiangning provincial treasurer, foreign affairs commissioner, and education commissioner; the Jiang-An grain transport, Jiangnan industrial promotion, constabulary, and salt control circuits; the Jiangning general and his deputy; and the imperial weaving office, which also supervised the Longjiang New Customs on the west.

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi, following the Ming system, it had eight counties.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Shunzhi it followed the Ming arrangement with eight counties.

sentences.zh: 雍正八年，改溧陽屬鎮江。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongzheng, Liyang was changed to belong to Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 8 Liyang was transferred to Zhenjiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 北距京師二千四百四十五里。

translations.literal: North, two thousand four hundred forty-five li from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: It lay 2,445 li north of the capital.

translations.literal: Its width was two hundred li and its length three hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: It measured 200 li from east to west and 300 li from north to south.

translations.literal: North polar altitude was thirty-two degrees four minutes.
translations.idiomatic: Its latitude was 32°04′ north.

sentences.zh: 京師偏東二度二十八分。

translations.literal: East of the capital by two degrees twenty-eight minutes.
translations.idiomatic: It lay 2°28′ east of the capital.

translations.literal: It governed seven counties.
translations.idiomatic: It administered seven counties.

translations.literal: Shangyuan: Vital, Busy, and Difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Shangyuan: Vital, Busy, and Difficult.

translations.literal: Attached.
translations.idiomatic: Attached seat.

sentences.zh: 附郭有清涼山、師子山、富貴山。

translations.literal: Within the attached prefectural seat were Qingliang Mountain, Shizi Mountain, and Fugui Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Within the prefectural seat lay Qingliang, Shizi, and Fugui mountains.

translations.literal: To the north: Purple Gold Mountain and Mufu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the north were Purple Gold Mountain and Mufu Mountain.

translations.literal: To the east: Wulong Mountain and Shengyou Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the east were Wulong Mountain and Shengyou Mountain.

sentences.zh: 有硃湖洞，道書三十一洞天。

translations.literal: There was Zhuhu Cave, the thirty-first grotto-heaven in Daoist texts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuhu Cave was listed in Daoist texts as the thirty-first grotto-heaven.

translations.literal: Inside Qingjiang Gate was Xiaocang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Inside Qingjiang Gate stood Xiaocang Mountain.

translations.literal: Inside Shicheng Gate was Yecheng Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Inside Shicheng Gate stood Yecheng Mountain.

sentences.zh: 南：大江自安徽當塗入，受秦淮河水，為草鞋夾。

translations.literal: To the south: the Great River entered from Dangtu in Anhui, received the Qinhuai River waters, and formed Caoxie Gorge.
translations.idiomatic: To the south the Yangtze entered from Dangtu in Anhui, took in the Qinhuai, and formed Caoxie Gorge.

sentences.zh: 左與江浦分岸，得觀音山水。

translations.literal: On the left it divided banks with Jiangpu and received Guanyin Mountain waters.
translations.idiomatic: On the left bank it bordered Jiangpu and received the waters of Guanyin Mountain.

translations.literal: There was Yanziji.
translations.idiomatic: Yanziji lay along the river.

sentences.zh: 秦淮河上承句容赤山湖水，合廬山水，逕通濟門，一入江寧，一入城。

translations.literal: The Qinhuai River upstream received Chishan Lake waters from Jurong, joined Lushan waters, passed straight through Tongji Gate — one branch entering Jiangning and one entering the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Qinhuai rose from Chishan Lake in Jurong, absorbed Lushan stream, and ran through Tongji Gate, one branch entering Jiangning and one entering the city wall.

translations.literal: It again flowed northwest and entered the river at Xiaguan.
translations.idiomatic: It then flowed northwest and entered the Yangtze at Xiaguan.

sentences.zh: 新開河東北，乾隆四十五年濬，賜名便民。

translations.literal: The newly opened canal to the northeast was dredged in the forty-fifth year of Qianlong and granted the name Bianmin (Convenience for the People).
translations.idiomatic: A newly opened canal to the northeast was dredged in Qianlong 45 and named the Bianmin Canal (Convenience for the People).

translations.literal: There was a market called Shipu Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: A market stood at Shipu Bridge.

translations.literal: Farther east was Huangtian Shoal.
translations.idiomatic: Farther east lay Huangtian Shoal.

sentences.zh: 鎮四：淳化、靖安、土橋、石步。

translations.literal: Four towns: Chunhua, Jing'an, Tuqiao, and Shibu.
translations.idiomatic: Its market towns were Chunhua, Jing'an, Tuqiao, and Shibu.

sentences.zh: 草鞋夾、燕子磯、棲霞街、湖熟有汛。

translations.literal: Caoxie Gorge, Yanziji, Qixia Street, and Hushu had garrison posts.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison posts were stationed at Caoxie Gorge, Yanziji, Qixia Street, and Hushu.

translations.literal: One courier station: Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: It had one courier station, Jinling.

translations.literal: Chunhua patrol office.
translations.idiomatic: A Chunhua patrol office was established.

translations.literal: There was a railway.
translations.idiomatic: A railway line served the county.

translations.literal: Trading port: Xiaguan.
translations.idiomatic: Its treaty port was Xiaguan.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十一年馬關條約四埠之一。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Guangxu it was one of the four ports under the Treaty of Shimonoseki.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 21 it became one of the four treaty ports opened under the Treaty of Shimonoseki.

translations.literal: Jiangning: Vital, Busy, and Difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangning: Vital, Busy, and Difficult.

translations.literal: Attached.
translations.idiomatic: Attached seat.

sentences.zh: 南：聚寶山雨花台設砲台。

translations.literal: To the south: on Jubao Mountain at Yuhuatai batteries were set up.
translations.idiomatic: To the south, batteries were built on Yuhuatai at Jubao Mountain.

translations.literal: The Great River passed directly through Xiaguan town.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangtze ran directly past Xiaguan town.

sentences.zh: 港七：銅井、烈山，北曰河口、綠新墅，又北大勝關，古新林浦也，西北曰北河，曰下關，分受秦淮河水。

translations.literal: Seven harbors: Tongjing and Lieshan; to the north called Hekou and Lvxin Villa; farther north Dasheng Pass, ancient Xinlin Ford; northwest called North River and Xiaguan, which separately received Qinhuai River waters.
translations.idiomatic: It had seven harbors—Tongjing and Lieshan; to the north Hekou and Lvxin Villa; farther north Dasheng Pass, the ancient Xinlin Ford; and to the northwest the North River and Xiaguan, which took separate branches of the Qinhuai.

translations.literal: Three towns: Jiangning, Moling, and Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Its market towns were Jiangning, Moling, and Jinling.

translations.literal: Dasheng and Moling had garrison posts.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison posts were stationed at Dasheng and Moling.

translations.literal: There was a courier station.
translations.idiomatic: It had a courier station.

translations.literal: Two patrol offices: Jiangning and Moling.
translations.idiomatic: Two patrol offices served Jiangning and Moling.

translations.literal: There was a railway.
translations.idiomatic: A railway line served the county.

translations.literal: Jurong: Vital and Difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Jurong: Vital and Difficult.

translations.literal: Ninety li east of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay ninety li east of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: The county had Jurong Mountain, from which it took its name.
translations.idiomatic: The county took its name from Jurong Mountain.

translations.literal: To the north: Hua Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the north stood Hua Mountain.

translations.literal: To the northeast: Tong Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the northeast stood Tong Mountain.

translations.literal: To the southeast: Mao Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the southeast stood Mao Mountain.

translations.literal: The Great River came from the east.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangtze approached from the east.

translations.literal: Two harbors: Luosi Ditch and Xiashu Harbor.
translations.idiomatic: It had two harbors, Luosi Ditch and Xiashu Harbor.

sentences.zh: 赤山湖出絳岩山，秦淮水源於此，亦曰絳岩湖。

translations.literal: Chishan Lake issued from Jiangyan Mountain; the Qinhuai River originated here, also called Jiangyan Lake.
translations.idiomatic: Chishan Lake rose on Jiangyan Mountain and was the source of the Qinhuai; it was also called Jiangyan Lake.

sentences.zh: 匯亭水、黃堰河、蒲里溪，曰南源，與北源合於白米湖，又西入上元。

translations.literal: Huiting Stream, Huangyan River, and Puli Brook were called the southern source; they joined the northern source at Baimi Lake and again flowed west into Shangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Huiting Stream, Huangyan River, and Puli Brook formed the southern source; with the northern source they met at Baimi Lake and then flowed west into Shangyuan.

sentences.zh: 鎮五：白土、常寧、東陽、下蜀、龍潭。

translations.literal: Five towns: Baitu, Changning, Dongyang, Xiashu, and Longtan.
translations.idiomatic: Its market towns were Baitu, Changning, Dongyang, Xiashu, and Longtan.

translations.literal: Longtan patrol office.
translations.idiomatic: A Longtan patrol office was established.

translations.literal: There was a courier station.
translations.idiomatic: It had a courier station.

translations.literal: Lishui: Simple.
translations.idiomatic: Lishui: Simple.

translations.literal: One hundred forty li southeast of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay 140 li southeast of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: To the south: Zhi Mountain and Zhong Mountain, also called Dushan.
translations.idiomatic: To the south were Zhi Mountain and Zhong Mountain, also known as Dushan.

sentences.zh: 東：廬山，秦淮水別源所出。

translations.literal: To the east: Lu Mountain, where a separate source of the Qinhuai issued.
translations.idiomatic: To the east stood Lu Mountain, source of a secondary branch of the Qinhuai.

sentences.zh: 石臼湖西南，逕城北流入秦淮，明故運道也，今淤。

translations.literal: Shijiu Lake to the southwest passed by the north of the city wall and flowed into the Qinhuai; it was the Ming-era transport canal, now silted up.
translations.idiomatic: Shijiu Lake to the southwest ran north of the city wall into the Qinhuai along the Ming transport canal, now silted up.

translations.literal: One courier station: Kongjia.
translations.idiomatic: It had one courier station, Kongjia.

translations.literal: Jiangpu: Vital.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangpu: Vital.

translations.literal: Forty li northwest of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay forty li northwest of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: To the northeast: Shisangong Mountain and Jiulian Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the northeast were Shisangong Mountain and Jiulian Mountain.

translations.literal: To the west: Longdong Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the west stood Longdong Mountain.

sentences.zh: 大江西南自安徽和州入，右與江寧分岸。

translations.literal: The Great River from the southwest entered from Hezhou in Anhui; on the right it divided banks with Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangtze entered from the southwest at Hezhou in Anhui, with Jiangning on the right bank.

sentences.zh: 為口四：曰烏江，曰老西江，曰新河，曰老河。

translations.literal: It formed four mouths: called Wujiang, Old Xijiang, New River, and Old River.
translations.idiomatic: It formed four mouths: Wujiang, Old Xijiang, New River, and Old River.

sentences.zh: 受浦子口河，東北入六合。

translations.literal: It received Puzikou River and entered Liuhe to the northeast.
translations.idiomatic: It received the Puzikou River and flowed northeast into Liuhe.

sentences.zh: 滁水右瀆自安徽滁州入，亦曰後河，東與來安分岸，復盡入境，曰前河，右出支津至東葛鎮，又東北逕岔河集，會沙河入六合。

translations.literal: The right branch of the Chu River entered from Chuzhou in Anhui, also called the Rear River; eastward it divided banks with Lai'an, then entirely entered the territory and was called the Front River; on the right a branch channel issued to Dongge town, then again passed northeast by Chaheji, joined the Sha River, and entered Liuhe.
translations.idiomatic: The right branch of the Chu River entered from Chuzhou in Anhui, also called the Rear River; eastward it bordered Lai'an, then ran wholly within the county as the Front River, sent a branch to Dongge town, and northeast of Chaheji joined the Sha River and entered Liuhe.

translations.literal: Three towns: Gaowang, Xiangquan, and Gecheng.
translations.idiomatic: Its market towns were Gaowang, Xiangquan, and Gecheng.

translations.literal: Two courier stations: Jianghuai and Dongge.
translations.idiomatic: It had two courier stations, Jianghuai and Dongge.

translations.literal: One Pukou patrol office.
translations.idiomatic: One Pukou patrol office was established.

translations.literal: Jianghuai had a courier station assistant; abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Jianghuai once had a courier station assistant, but the post was abolished.

translations.literal: There was a railway.
translations.idiomatic: A railway line served the county.

translations.literal: Liuhe: Simple.
translations.idiomatic: Liuhe: Simple.

translations.literal: One hundred twenty li north of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay 120 li north of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: To the south: Guabu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the south stood Guabu Mountain.

translations.literal: To the southwest: Jinwang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the southwest stood Jinwang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 大江西南自江浦入，右與上元分岸。

translations.literal: The Great River from the southwest entered from Jiangpu; on the right it divided banks with Shangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangtze entered from the southwest at Jiangpu, with Shangyuan on the right bank.

sentences.zh: 折東南為通江集口支津，北抵城隍湖。

translations.literal: It turned southeast as the Tongjiangji mouth branch channel, reaching Chenghuang Lake to the north.
translations.idiomatic: It turned southeast as a branch at Tongjiangji mouth and reached Chenghuang Lake to the north.

translations.literal: There was a Shazhouwei fort battery.
translations.idiomatic: A fort battery stood at Shazhouwei.

translations.literal: Further east: Huazikou.
translations.idiomatic: Further east lay Huazikou.

sentences.zh: 滁河西自江浦入，逕皁河口，北為汊河，又南屈曲流入江。

translations.literal: The Chu River entered from the west at Jiangpu, passed straight through Zaohekou, became Chabe River to the north, then wound south and entered the river.
translations.idiomatic: The Chu River entered from Jiangpu in the west, passed Zaohekou, formed Chabe River to the north, then bent southward into the Yangtze.

translations.literal: The tax bureau commissioner was stationed.
translations.idiomatic: A tax bureau commissioner was stationed there.

sentences.zh: 鎮四：瓜步、長蘆、宣化、竹鎮。

translations.literal: Four towns: Guabu, Changlu, Xuanhua, and Zhuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: It had four market towns: Guabu, Changlu, Xuanhua, and Zhuzhen.

translations.literal: There had been a Tangyi courier station assistant; abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Tangyi once had a courier station assistant, but the post was abolished.

translations.literal: One Guabu patrol office.
translations.idiomatic: One Guabu patrol office was established.

translations.literal: Gaochun: Simple.
translations.idiomatic: Gaochun: Simple.

translations.literal: Two hundred forty li southeast of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay 240 li southeast of the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 大江，城北逕孩溪，復南繞圌山，分支為大小夾江，有寶晉、天福、補沙諸洲。

translations.literal: The great river north of the city passed Haixi, again south encircled Tushan, branched into great and small channel rivers, and had Baojin, Tianfu, Busha, and other isles.
translations.idiomatic: The great river north of the city passed Haixi, then wound south around Tushan and branched into great and small channel rivers, with isles including Baojin, Tianfu, and Busha.

sentences.zh: 運河南自丹陽入，逕雩山西、洪山東，折西環城北流，所謂南運河。

translations.literal: The Grand Canal south entered from Danyang, passed west of Yushan and east of Hongshan, bent west to encircle the city and flow north, the so-called Southern Grand Canal.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Canal entered from Danyang in the south, passed west of Yushan and east of Hongshan, bent west to encircle the city, and formed the so-called Southern Grand Canal.

sentences.zh: 糧艘渡江入伊婁河，至邗溝，為北運河，併入於江。

translations.literal: Grain ships crossed the river to enter Yilou River, reached Hangou, forming the Northern Grand Canal, and merged into the river.
translations.idiomatic: Grain ships crossed the river into Yilou River and reached Hangou as the Northern Grand Canal, which then merged into the river.

translations.literal: Hengyue had an assistant official.
translations.idiomatic: Hengyue had an assistant official.

sentences.zh: 西：高資河，東西與新開河合。

translations.literal: To the west: Gaozi River, east and west joined Xinkai River.
translations.idiomatic: To the west, Gaozi River joined Xinkai River from east and west.

sentences.zh: 河為乾隆四十五年巡撫吳壇濬，出排灣西經高資入句容。

translations.literal: The river was dredged in Qianlong 45 by Governor Wu Tan, exiting west of Paiwan, passing Gaozi to enter Jurong.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Wu Tan dredged the river in Qianlong 45; it exited west of Paiwan, passed through Gaozi, and entered Jurong.

sentences.zh: 商埠，縣北二里，外國互市租界，咸豐十年英法條約長江三口之一。

translations.literal: Commercial port, two li north of the county, foreign treaty-port concession, one of the three Yangtze ports in the Anglo-French treaty of Xianfeng 10.
translations.idiomatic: A commercial port two li north of the county served as a foreign treaty-port concession, one of the three Yangtze ports opened under the Anglo-French treaty of Xianfeng 10.

translations.literal: There was a new customs office, supervised by the Chang-Jiang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: A new customs office was supervised by the Chang-Jiang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 鎮五：丹徒、高資、諫壁、大港、新豐。

translations.literal: Five towns: Dantu, Gaozi, Jianbi, Dagang, and Xinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: It had five market towns: Dantu, Gaozi, Jianbi, Dagang, and Xinfeng.

translations.literal: Zhujiawei had a garrison post.
translations.idiomatic: A garrison post was stationed at Zhujiawei.

translations.literal: Two courier stations: Jingkou and Tanzhu.
translations.idiomatic: It had two courier stations: Jingkou and Tanzhu.

translations.literal: Jingkou had a courier-station assistant, abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Jingkou once had a courier-station assistant, later abolished.

translations.literal: Three patrol offices: Gaozi, Angang, and Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: Three patrol offices were established: Gaozi, Angang, and Dantu.

translations.literal: There was a railway.
translations.idiomatic: A railway line served the county.

translations.literal: Danyang: Busy, Exhausted, Difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Danyang: Busy, Exhausted, Difficult.

translations.literal: Seventy li southeast of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay 70 li southeast of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: To the northeast was Jiuling Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling Mountain lay to the northeast.

sentences.zh: 大江北自丹徒播為夾江，逕姚家橋入，東與江合。

translations.literal: The great river north from Dantu spread into channel rivers, passed Yaojia Bridge to enter, east joined the river.
translations.idiomatic: The great river north from Dantu spread into channel rivers, entered through Yaojia Bridge, and rejoined the main channel to the east.

sentences.zh: 運河東南逕七里橋，漕河會之。

translations.literal: The Grand Canal southeast passed Qili Bridge, and the grain canal joined it.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Canal passed southeast through Qili Bridge, where the grain canal joined it.

translations.literal: Again southwest spread into Xiangcao River.
translations.idiomatic: Farther southwest it spread into Xiangcao River.

translations.literal: Jiandu River encircled the city and flowed, entering the river.
translations.idiomatic: Jiandu River encircled the city and entered the river.

sentences.zh: 包港東北導運河水與夾江合。

translations.literal: Baogang northeast guided Grand Canal water to join the channel river.
translations.idiomatic: Baogang northeast guided Grand Canal water to join the channel river.

translations.literal: To the north was Lianhu.
translations.idiomatic: Lianhu lay to the north.

translations.literal: Two towns: Lücheng and Yanling.
translations.idiomatic: It had two market towns: Lücheng and Yanling.

translations.literal: One courier station: Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: It had one courier station, Yunyang.

translations.literal: Two patrol offices: Lücheng and Baogang.
translations.idiomatic: Two patrol offices were established: Lücheng and Baogang.

translations.literal: There was a railway.
translations.idiomatic: A railway line served the county.

translations.literal: Jintan: Exhausted, Difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Jintan: Exhausted, Difficult.

translations.literal: One hundred sixty li south of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay 160 li south of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: To the west: Maoshan, also called Sanmao Peak.
translations.idiomatic: To the west lay Maoshan, also called Sanmao Peak.

sentences.zh: 南：長盪湖，與溧陽錯，古洮湖也。

translations.literal: To the south: Changdang Lake, interlocking with Liyang, the ancient Taohu.
translations.idiomatic: To the south lay Changdang Lake, interlocking with Liyang, the ancient Taohu.

sentences.zh: 漕河環城為濠，南會於白龍盪，又南受湖水入溧陽。

translations.literal: The grain canal encircled the city as a moat, south met at Bailong Marsh, again south received lake water to enter Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: The grain canal encircled the city as a moat, met Bailong Marsh in the south, and farther south took lake water into Liyang.

sentences.zh: 薛步水出薛步鎮，東流分為二，一入漕河，一南與漕河遇，入於湖。

translations.literal: Xuebu water exited Xuebu Town, flowed east and split into two, one entered the grain canal, one south met the grain canal and entered the lake.
translations.idiomatic: Xuebu water rose at Xuebu Town, flowed east, and split in two, one branch entering the grain canal and one meeting it in the south before entering the lake.

translations.literal: To the east was Qianzi Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzi Marsh lay to the east.

translations.literal: One Huxi patrol office, abolished.
translations.idiomatic: One Huxi patrol office was established, later abolished.

translations.literal: Liyang: Busy, Exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Liyang: Busy, Exhausted.

translations.literal: Two hundred forty li south of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay 240 li south of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: In Yongzheng 8 came to be subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 8 it was placed under the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 西：曹姥山、鐵冶山一曰鐵峴。

translations.literal: To the west: Caolao Mountain, Tieye Mountain also called Tiexian.
translations.idiomatic: To the west lay Caolao Mountain and Tieye Mountain, also called Tiexian.

sentences.zh: 北：涪山，峙洮湖中，湖與金壇錯。

translations.literal: To the north: Fushan, standing in Taohu, the lake interlocking with Jintan.
translations.idiomatic: To the north, Fushan stood in Taohu, a lake interlocking with Jintan.

sentences.zh: 三塔盪西南溢為昇平盪。

translations.literal: Santan Marsh southwest overflowed into Shengping Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: Santan Marsh overflowed southwest into Shengping Marsh.

sentences.zh: 前馬盪水出溧水廬山，合高淳諸水，東逕為盪入中河，東南流與漕河合，古中江也。

translations.literal: Qianma Marsh water exited Lishui Lushan, joined Gaochun waters, east passed as marsh into Zhonghe, flowed southeast to join the grain canal, the ancient Middle River.
translations.idiomatic: Qianma Marsh water rose at Lushan in Lishui, joined waters from Gaochun, passed east as a marsh into Zhonghe, flowed southeast to join the grain canal, and was the ancient Middle River.

sentences.zh: 五代楊行密築五堰，江自是不復東，禹跡中湮矣。

translations.literal: In the Five Dynasties Yang Xingmi built the Five Weirs, and from then the river no longer flowed east; the trace of Yu in the Middle River was silted away.
translations.idiomatic: In the Five Dynasties Yang Xingmi built the Five Weirs, after which the river no longer flowed east and the course of Yu's Middle River was lost.

translations.literal: Three towns: Jushan, Piqiao, and Guangdao.
translations.idiomatic: It had three market towns: Jushan, Piqiao, and Guangdao.
